text:
chandra: Heads-up — ingest-lambda started seeing AccessDenied on KMS Decrypt after yesterday's key rotation. Error in app logs: "User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ingest-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345"
alice: ugh. Is this for envelope-encrypted payloads (data key wrapped by KMS)?
chandra: yes, we encrypt data keys with the customer master key and store ciphertext. The lambda loads envelope, calls KMS Decrypt with CiphertextBlob + GrantToken from prior grant. Worked before rotation. :thinking_face:
ben: first things: confirm the rotated key's key policy still allows the ingest-role, and check any grants were re-created or invalidated by rotation. Rotation can revoke grants depending on how you rotated (rekey vs new CMK).
alice: I pulled CloudTrail event for KMS Decrypt and it shows "errorCode": "AccessDeniedException" and the requestParameters show no grantId. Also saw a RevokeGrant for a grantId around the rotation time.
chandra: oh that explains it. The code expects a grant token passed in. If RevokeGrant removed the grant, passing the token won't help. We either need to recreate a grant or rely on key policy/IAM.
ben: quick checklist: 1) aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <key-id> — verify key policy allows kms:Decrypt for arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role or the assumed-role principal. 2) Confirm role trust & session principal format: CloudWatch logs show "assumed-role/ingest-role/session"; in key policy you might need the role ARN (not the assumed principal). 3) If you're using grants, run aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id> and aws kms list-retirable-grants --key-id <key-id> as the key account.
alice: I checked get-key-policy — the policy references a principal: { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role" } — should be fine. But the decrypt was attempted by an assumed role session, so a principal like arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ingest-role/session. Is that mismatch relevant?
chandra: No, IAM evaluates the role ARN equivalently for role-based permissions, but key policy is evaluated for the principal in the request. For KMS, the role ARN is acceptable. More likely the grant revocation killed the allowed path. Also check for kms:ViaService or aws:SourceArn conditions in the key policy that might be blocking Decrypt from Lambda if it expects a different service principal.
ben: to reproduce locally: 1) aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role --role-session-name testSession 2) export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/... from credentials 3) aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --key-id <key-id>  (if grant needed: --grant-tokens <token>)  Observe AccessDenied.
alice: ran that and got the same AccessDenied. Next I tried creating a new grant from the key account:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id <key-id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role --operations Decrypt --name temp-ingest-grant
```
Then used the returned GrantId token in the lambda call flow and decrypt succeeded.
chandra: OK so grants were required in our setup — maybe the original key rotation process created a new CMK and we re-pointed data to it but didn't recreate grants. 
ben: couple of notes for long-term fix: - Recreate required grants as part of rotation automation (or avoid rotation method that revokes grants if you rely on them). - Prefer key-policy + IAM allow path for roles instead of ephemeral grants when possible (simpler to reason about). - If you must use grants, store grantIds and refresh on rotation and make grant creation idempotent.
alice: also discovered the lambda code was passing an old grant-token header (from env var) even after rotation; when grant was revoked, that confused debugging. Removing the token and relying on role/IAM permits worked once we adjusted key policy.
chandra: action items: 1) infra: update rotation runbook to re-create grants and/or update key-policy; include test steps that assume-role and call aws kms decrypt. 2) devs: stop persisting grant tokens in env; instead request fresh grant or use IAM path. 3) ops: run a one-off script to list keys recently rotated and check for missing grants for expected roles.
kms-bot: Automated check finished — for key abcd-ef01-2345 found RevokeGrant event at 1987653000, no current grants for grantee arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role.
ben: I'll open a tiny PR to rotation scripts and add the test. chandra — can you paste the minimal repro commands and the grant create snippet into the runbook?
chandra: pasted and updated runbook. Snippet included: ```sh
# repro assume and decrypt
CREDS=$(aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role --role-session-name repro)
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo $CREDS | jq -r .Credentials.AccessKeyId)
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo $CREDS | jq -r .Credentials.SecretAccessKey)
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo $CREDS | jq -r .Credentials.SessionToken)
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```
chandra: also noted: if you rely on encryption context, ensure the lambda supplies the same context when decrypting. Mismatched encryption context also causes AccessDenied even when policy allows Decrypt.
alice: thanks all. I'll run the rotation audit script across prod keys and report back by EOD. :thumbsup:
